ref: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
text: Mɔlebɛbo ne Nyamenle bɔle anwuma nee aze.

ref: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
text: Ɛnee azɛlɛ ye ɛnzɔho ɛhwee, yɛɛ debie biala ɛnle zolɛ; awozinli ɛheda buma ne anye, na Nyamenle Sunsum ne luolua nzule ne anye.

ref: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
text: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Wienyi ɛrɛla”; na wienyi rale.

ref: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
text: Nyamenle nwunle kɛ wienyi ne le kpalɛ, na ɔdele wienyi ne ɔvile awozinli ne anwo.

ref: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
text: Nyamenle vɛlɛle wienyi ne “Alehyenlɛ” yɛɛ ɔvɛlɛle awozinli ne “Aledwolɛ”. Akee aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle. Ɛhye a le kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la.

ref: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
text: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Anwomanyunlu ɛrɛla ɛrade nzule ne mɔ avinli.”

ref: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
text: Na ɔvɛlɛle anwomanyunlu “Anwuma.” Aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle; kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nwiɔ la ɛne.

ref: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
text: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Nzule mɔɔ wɔ ewiade la ɛhɔ ɛleka ko ɛye ɛleka resee ɛdo ɛkɛ.” Na ɔyɛle zɔhane.

ref: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
text: Nyamenle vɛlɛle ɛleka resee ne “Azɛlɛ”, yɛɛ ɔvɛlɛle nzule ne mɔ mɔɔ hɔle ɛleka ko la “Nyevile”. Na Nyamenle nwunle kɛ ɔle kpalɛ.

ref: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
text: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Ɛbɔ ɛrɛla azɛlɛ ye azo; ndile nee mbaka mɔɔ so ma, yɛɛ nzoleɛ mbaka mɔɔ ma wɔ bɛ nzoleɛ ne mɔ anu la, ko biala nee ye ɛsaso ɛrɛla.” Na ɔyɛle zɔhane.

ref: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
text: Ndile nee mbaka ngakyile kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ so ma, yɛɛ nzoleɛ mbaka mɔɔ ma wɔ bɛ nzoleɛ ne mɔ anu la, ko biala nee ye ɛsaso, fifile azɛlɛ ye azo. Na Nyamenle nwunle kɛ ɔle kpalɛ.

ref: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
text: Aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle; kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsa la ɛne.

ref: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
text: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Ahɛnlaneɛ ɛrɛla anwomanyunlu anwuma lɔ, ɛrade alehyenlɛ nee aledwolɛ avinli, na bɛyɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ mɔɔ kile ɛlobɔ, kenle, nee ɛvolɛ a,

ref: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
text: na bɛda anwomanyunlu anwuma lɔ bɛmaa wienyi ɛrɛla azɛlɛ ye azo.” Na ɔyɛle zɔhane.

ref: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
text: Na Nyamenle yɛle anwuma ahɛnlaneɛ mgbole nwiɔ ne, ɔyɛle kpole kpalɛ ne, sɛnzɛne ne, kɛ ɔda alehyenlɛ nu; akee ɔyɛle kpole ekyi ne, siane ne, kɛ ɔda aledwolɛ nu. Ɔyɛle nwɔlɔra noko.

ref: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
text: Ɔyɛle ɛhye mɔ ɔzieziele anwomanyunlu anwuma lɔ kɛ bɛda bɛmaa wienyi ɛrɛla azɛlɛ ye azo.

ref: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
text: Ɔyɛle kɛ bɛda alehyenlɛ nee aledwolɛ nu, amaa bɛade wienyi ne bɛavi awozinli ne anwo. Na Nyamenle nwunle mɔɔ yeyɛ la kɛ ɔle kpalɛ.

ref: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
text: Aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle; kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nna la ɛne.

ref: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
text: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Nzule nu anyewɔzo abɔdeɛ ngakyile muala ɛrɛla, na nloma mɔɔ tu dua anwomanyunlu la ɛrɛla.”

ref: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
text: Yemɔti Nyamenle bɔle nyevile nu abɔdeɛ mgbole anwo ɛzulolɛ muala nee nzule nu anyewɔzo abɔdeɛ biala nee bɛ ɛsaso, nee nloma kɔsɔɔti nee bɛ ɛsaso. Na Nyamenle nwunle kɛ ɔle kpalɛ.

ref: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
text: Nyamenle yilale bɛ muala na ɔzele kɛ, “Bɛlɔ, bɛyɛ dɔɔnwo bɛyi azule nee nyevile,” na ɔzele nloma noko kɛ, “Bɛdabɛ bɛda, bɛyɛ mɔnwo mɔnwo wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo.”

ref: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
text: Aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle; kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nnu la ɛne.

ref: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
text: Akee Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Anyewɔzo abɔdeɛ ɛrɛla azɛlɛ ye azo, biala nee ye ɛsaso: nlankɛ nee ninyɛne mɔɔ twenle bɛ nwo aze la amuala nee nanemgbole, ko biala nee ye ɛsaso.” Na ɔyɛle zɔhane.

ref: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
text: Na Nyamenle bɔle azɛlɛ ye azo nanemgbole, ko biala nee ye ɛsaso: nlankɛ nee ninyɛne mɔɔ twenle bɛ nwo aze la amuala, ko biala nee ye ɛsaso. Na Nyamenle nwunle kɛ ɔle kpalɛ.

ref: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
text: Akee Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Bɛmaa yɛyɛ sonla kɛ yɛdayɛ yɛ ɛsaso yɛmaa ɔzɔho yɛ, na yɛmaa bɛnlea azule nee nyevile nu fɛlɛ, nloma mɔɔ wɔ anwomanyunlu, nyɛmoa nee nanemgbole nee debie biala mɔɔ twenle ɔ nwo aze wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo la anwo zo.”

ref: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
text: Yemɔti Nyamenle bɔle sonla kɛ ɔdaye ye ɛsaso la; ɔdaye Nyamenle mumua ne ye ɛsaso a ɔnleanle ɔbɔle sonla a. Ɔbɔle bɛ nrenya nee raalɛ.

ref: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
text: Na Nyamenle yilale bɛ, na ɔzele kɛ, “Bɛlɔ, bɛyɛ mɔnwo mɔnwo, bɛyi azɛlɛ ye na bɛzie azɛlɛ ye. Eza bɛzie azule nee nyevile nu fɛlɛ, anwomanyunlu nloma nee azɛlɛ ye azo abɔdeɛ biala mɔɔ die ɛnwomenle la.”

ref: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
text: Meva ndile muala noko memaa debie biala mɔɔ lɛ ngoane wɔ ye nuhua: azɛlɛ ye azo nane kɔsɔɔti nee anwomanyunlu nloma nee ninyɛne mɔɔ twenle bɛ nwo aze la amuala kɛ bɛli.” Na ɔyɛle zɔhane.

ref: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
text: Na Nyamenle nwunle kɛ debie biala mɔɔ yeyɛ la le kpalɛ kpole. Aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle; kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsia la ɛne.

ref: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
text: Ɛnee kɛ Nyamenle zile bɔle anwuma nee aze, nee ninyɛne mɔɔ wɔ nu la amuala la ɛne.

ref: That's how God created the heavens and the earth. The Garden of Eden When the Lord God made the heavens and the earth,
text: Ɛnee kɛ Nyamenle zile bɔle anwuma nee aze la ɛne. Yidɛn tola ne Mekɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle bɔle anwuma nee azɛlɛ ye la,

ref: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
text: ɛnee baka biala ɛngyi azɛlɛ ye azo, yɛɛ ndile biala ɛtɛfifile, ɔluakɛ ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle ɛtɛmanle ezule ɛtɛtɔle azɛlɛ ye azo, yɛɛ ɛnee sonla ɛnle zolɛ na yeazo zolɛ ɛya.

ref: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
text: Noko ɛnee nzule vi azɛlɛ bo finde bu azɛlɛ ne azo amuala tɛloo.

ref: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
text: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle vale ndɛtɛlɛ nwonle sonla na ɔliele ngoane ɛnwomenle ɔguale ɔ bonyi nu, na sonla nyianle ngoane.

ref: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
text: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle hyele tola wɔ Yidɛn, wɔ aduduleɛ nehane, na ɔmanle sonla ne mɔɔ yebɔ la dɛnlanle ɛkɛ.

ref: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
text: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle manle mbaka kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ le ngɛnlɛma nee mɔɔ bɛdi a ɔyɛ boɛ la fifile; ɔmanle ngoane baka ne yɛɛ baka ne mɔɔ maa ɛkola ɛnwu kpalɛ nee ɛtane la ɔdaye bɛfifile tola ne anu.

ref: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
text: Azule la Yidɛn na ɔse ɔdoɔloa tola ne anu. Azule ne dwu tola ne anu a, ɔkpakye nna.

ref: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
text: Bɛfɛlɛ azule ne asa ɛhane ne mɔɔ lumua la Paehyɔn; ɔse ɔdua Havelaa azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ezukoa nvutuke wɔ zolɛ la azo.

ref: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
text: Azule ne asa ɛhane ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nwiɔ la, bɛfɛlɛ ye Gaehyɔn; ɔse ɔdua Kɛhye azɛlɛ ne azo.

ref: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
text: Mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsa la, bɛfɛlɛ ye Taegelese; ɔse ɔdua Aselea maanle ne aduduleɛ, yɛɛ mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nna la, bɛfɛlɛ ye Yufileti.

ref: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
text: Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle manle sonla hɔdɛnlanle Yidɛn tola ne anu kɛ ɔyɛ nu egyinli na ɔziezie ɛkɛ.

ref: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
text: Ɔzele ye kɛ, “Ɛkola ɛdi bakama biala mɔɔ wɔ tola ye anu la bie,

ref: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
text: na kpalɛ nee ɛtane ɛnwunlɛ baka ne, yemɔ mmadi ye ma ne bie, ɔluakɛ kenle ko ne mɔɔ ɛkɛli bie la, ɛbawu.”

ref: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
text: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Ɔnle kpalɛ kɛ menwɔmaa sonla angomekye kɛdɛnla; mebabɔ ye ɛsaso boavolɛ meamaa ye.”

ref: So the Lord took some soil and made animals and birds. He brought them to the man to see what names he would give each of them. Then the man named the tame animals and the birds and the wild animals. That's how they got their names. None of these was the right kind of partner for the man.
text: Sonla totonle nyɛmoa ne mɔ aluma ngoko ngoko, ɔtotonle nloma mɔɔ tu dua anwomanyunlu la aluma yɛɛ ɔtotonle nanemgbole mɔɔ wɔ ɛbɔ nu la aluma. Na ɔdaye sonla ɛdeɛ, yeannyia ye ɛsaso boavolɛ biala.

ref: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
text: Yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle manle sonla lafele kpole bie na ɔyele ɔ nvenle foa bowule ko na ɔvale nwonane ɔduale ɔ bo zo ne.

ref: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
text: Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle vale bowule ne mɔɔ ɔyele la ɔyɛle sonla raalɛ na ɔvale ye ɔrɛlɛle nrenya ne.

ref: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
text: Na nrenya ne zele kɛ, Ɛhye le me mbowule nu bowule, ɔle me nwonane nu nwonane; bɛbavɛlɛ ye “Raalɛ”, ɔboalekɛ ɔvi sonla nrenya nu a ɔrale a.

ref: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
text: Yemɔti a nrenya fi ɔ ze nee ɔ nli anwo na ɔfa ɔ nwo ɔbɔ ɔ ye anwo kyengye, na bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛbɔ nu bɛyɛ nwonane ko a.

ref: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
text: Ɛnee nrenya ne nee ɔ ye ne lɛ bɛ nwo zɔ, noko bɛnze nwolɛ nyiane.

ref: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
text: Ɛwɔlɛ le mɛlɛbɛla tɛla ɛbɔ nu nane biala mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle bɔle la. Ɔbizale raalɛ ne kɛ, “Yemɔti Nyamenle ɛze bɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛmmadi mbakama mɔɔ wɔ tola ye anu la biala bie’ ɔ?”

ref: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
text: Raalɛ ne buale ɛwɔlɛ ne kɛ, “Yɛkola yɛdi mbakama mɔɔ wɔ tola ye anu la biala bie;

ref: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
text: na Nyamenle zele yɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛmmadi baka ne mɔɔ gyi tola ne avinli lɔ la ma ne bie, eza bɛmmafa bɛ sa bɛka ye anrɛɛ bɛkɛwu.’ ”

ref: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
text: Ɛwɔlɛ ne hanle hilele raalɛ ne kɛ, “Bɛnrɛwu.

ref: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
text: Nyamenle ze kɛ saa bɛdi baka ne ma ne bie a bɛ nye babuke na bɛayɛ kɛ ɔdaye Nyamenle la, na bɛanwu mɔɔ le kpalɛ, bɛannwu mɔɔ le ɛtane la.”

ref: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
text: Yemɔti mɔɔ raalɛ ne nwunle kɛ baka ne ma ne le kɛnlɛma, na bɛdi a ɔle kpalɛ, na ɔwɔ kɛ sonla di bie na ɔnwu nrɛlɛbɛ la, ɔdele bie ɔlile, na ɔdele bie ɔhɔmanle ɔ hu lile.

ref: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
text: Ɛkɛ ne ala bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛ nye dele na bɛnwunle kɛ bɛlɛ bɛ nwo zɔ; bɛkpomgbale feege nya bɛwowale bɛ nwo.

ref: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
text: Nzinlii mɔɔ aleɛ ne bɔle ɔ nloa aze la, bɛdele Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle agyakɛ abo kɛ ɔlɛkpɔsa tola ne anu, na bɛnriandile bɛhɔveale tola ne anu mbaka ne mɔ anu, amaa yeannwu bɛ.

ref: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
text: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle vɛlɛle nrenya ne na ɔbizale ye kɛ, “Ɛwɔ nienwu?”

ref: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
text: Nrenya ne buale kɛ, “Mendele ɛ gyakɛ abo wɔ tola ne anu, na ɛnee mesulo, ɔboalekɛ melɛ me nwo zɔ, yɛɛ menveale a.”

ref: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
text: Nyamenle bizale ye kɛ, “Nwane a hanle hilele wɔ kɛ ɛlɛ ɛ nwo zɔ a? Ɛnee wɔli bakama ne mɔɔ menduale wɔ kɛ ɛmmadi bie la bie ɔ?”

ref: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
text: Nrenya ne buale kɛ, “Raalɛ ne mɔɔ ɛvale ye ɛmanle me la, yemɔ a vale manle me a, yɛɛ menlile a.”

ref: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
text: Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle bizale raalɛ ne kɛ, “Duzu debie a wɔyɛ la?” Raalɛ ne buale kɛ, “Ɛwɔlɛ ne bɛlɛbɛlale me, lile me adwenle yɛɛ menlile bie a.” Nyamenle bua ndɛne

ref: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
text: Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle zele ɛwɔlɛ ne kɛ, “Ɔlua ɛhye mɔɔ wɔyɛ la ati, munzule ɛha wɔ wɔ nyɛmoa nee nanemgbole kɔsɔɔti avinli. Ɔvi ɛnɛ mɔɔ kɔ la ɛbahwenle ɛ ko aze na wɔali ndɛtɛlɛ kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ ɛkɛwu la.

ref: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
text: Mebava ɛkpɔlɛ meado wɔ nee raalɛ ne, nee ɛ ra nee raalɛ ne ara avinli. Raalɛ ne ara bagelegele ɛ ti na ɛdawɔ wɔaha ɔ gyakɛ anzi.”

ref: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
text: Akee ɔzele raalɛ ne kɛ, “Mebamaa wɔade nyane kpalɛ wɔ awolɛ nu; ɛbade nyane wɔ wɔ ralɛ ɛwolɛ nu, noko ɛ nwo balɔ ɛ hu na yeazie wɔ.”

ref: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
text: Na ɔzele Adam kɛ, “Kɛmɔ wɔdie ɛ ye aneɛ na wɔli bakama ne mɔɔ menzele wɔ kɛ ɛmmadi la bie la ati, ɔlua ɛ ti, munzule ɛha azɛlɛ ye; ɛtɛwule a ɛbavɛ na wɔanyia aleɛ wɔali.

ref: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
text: Mbaka nee ndile mɔɔ anwo le mbowule la bafifi azɛlɛ ye azo, noko ɛbɔ nu ala a ɛbadidi a.

ref: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
text: Ɛbahwi ɛ ti anwo na wɔanyia aleɛ wɔali, kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ ɛkɛzia ɛkɛhɔ azɛlɛ ye anu bieko la, ɔluakɛ nuhua yɛɛ ɛvi ɛrale a; ɛle ndɛtɛlɛ na ɛbazia wɔahɔ ndɛtɛlɛ nu.”

ref: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
text: Ɛhye anzi, nrenya ne donle ɔ ye duma na ɔvɛlɛle ye Yive, ɔboalekɛ ɔle menli kɔsɔɔti bɛ nli.

ref: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
